newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Prairie seeding 69 pct done May 26 - CWB.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Prairie seeding 69 pct done May 26 - CWB.

text.p: Spring seeding of Canada's six major grains and oilseeds was 69 percent complete by Monday, a Canadian Wheat Board weather analyst said.
"Alberta's ahead of the game. Saskatchewan and Manitoba were about the same," CWB weather and crop surveillance director Paul Bullock said.
All wheat seeded area on the Prairies was seen 9.2 percent down at 28.22 million acres in 1997 from 31.08 million acres the year before, Statistics Canada said April 30.
Canola area was forecast up 32 percent to 11.585 million acres from 8.8 million, StatsCan said.
"Manitoba's further along than expected so that's good news. The area restricted by flooding has shrunk. The bigger concern is in Alberta's Peace River Valley," Bullock said.
About a half million acres of southern Manitoba's farmland was flooded when the Red River crested earlier this month at its highest level in 145 years.
Cold, wet weather impeded harvest of crops left standing last fall as well as seeding in Alberta's Peace River Valley.
"The Peace River's 20 to 30 percent seeded. There's more area there than what's flooded in the Red River Valley at this time," Bullock said.
No regions reported killing frosts overnight, Environment Canada said.

Wheat needs 90 to 100 days to mature. Barley needs 60 to 90 days to mature, oats 85 to 88 days, flax 85 to 100 days, Argentine canola 92 to 102 days, Polish canola 73 to 83 days and field peas 90 to 100 days.
The average spring frost season for the Prairies ends between May 20 and 28, Bullock said.
Lows of -4.0 Celsius must last four hours to kill wheat but spring crops can be reseeded.
